$comment: Mount-plane cases (coord_frame_contract section 3.4). Each tool that computes z runs them in its own tests; the reference readers compute no z and do not. outcome is accept (nothing to seat), seat or refuse; warns says whether the tool warns about the file; dies gives each die's expected bottom z. In the first four no die names a connection, so a die computed by the rule sits on the plane itself. In the explicit_z cases each die names the file's 44 um connection stack and writes its z; a tool keeps it, and an exporter refuses a z other than the file's plane plus that height. A viewer may report that mismatch; warns is left out where the rule leaves it to the tool. Every interposer is 200 thick, so only the plane varies. stackup_plane is the plane the technology's stackup (case data) gives, which the file's value overrides.
